intro: Ben Rice went nuclear in the MLB playoff opener as the Yankees bludgeoned the Red Sox 9-0, and it wasn't even close. Meanwhile, the NBA brought the hammer down on the Clippers over the Kawhi Leonard investigation, and the league isn't playing around.

stories.headline: Ben Rice Goes Nuclear: Yankees Bludgeon Red Sox 9-0 in Playoff Opener
stories.body: Ben Rice went off for six RBIs — including a grand slam in the eighth — as the Yankees dismantled the Red Sox 9-0 in Game 1, with Cam Schlittler dealing 6 1/3 shutout innings to set the tone. New York swept the series by Wednesday, which is exactly the kind of October the Red Sox were hoping to avoid.

stories.headline: Michael King Nearly Makes History, Padres Blank Cubs 8-0
stories.body: Michael King took a no-hitter into the seventh inning as San Diego steamrolled Chicago 8-0 in Game 1, then finished off the sweep to punch their Division Series ticket. The Cubs managed to avoid the no-no but couldn't avoid getting bounced in three.

stories.headline: Austin Riley Saves Atlanta, But the Phillies Aren't Dead Yet
stories.body: Riley's three-run bomb in the eighth gave the Braves a 5-3 Game 1 win, but Philadelphia came right back to take Game 2 and force a deciding Game 3. Someone's postseason is ending in Atlanta this week.

stories.headline: Washington's Season Is Crumbling: Mariota Out, Lane Likely Done
stories.body: Marcus Mariota left Sunday's London loss to the Colts with a knee injury, and WR Jaylin Lane is reportedly done for the season after fracturing and dislocating his ankle. The Commanders are officially in crisis mode before October is even a week old.

stories.headline: Drake Maye and the Patriots Just Upset the Bills in Buffalo
stories.body: New England pulled off one of Week 4's biggest shockers, knocking off the Bills in Buffalo behind a strong showing from Drake Maye. Mike Vrabel says his concern level is still "very high" — which somehow makes the win feel more ominous for everyone else.

stories.headline: Tyreek Hill to Kansas City? His Agent Says a Deal Could Happen Any Day
stories.body: The Chiefs are reportedly interested in bringing Tyreek Hill back, and agent Drew Rosenhaus told NBC Sports he expects Hill to sign with a team within days. Patrick Mahomes getting his old weapon back is the kind of rumor that should make the rest of the AFC nervous.

stories.headline: NBA Absolutely Destroys the Clippers Over Kawhi Leonard Investigation
stories.body: The league dropped the hammer on Los Angeles, stripping the Clippers of 5 first-round picks and slapping them with a $30 million fine in the Kawhi Leonard probe. Rough time to also announce Brandon Ingram is starting the season with a partially torn Achilles.

stories.headline: LeBron James Is a 76er Now — and He Wanted to Be a Knick
stories.body: LeBron showed up to his first Philly media day and casually admitted he had wanted to sign with New York before landing in Philadelphia. The Knicks fan base will be fine, probably.

stories.headline: Jalen Duren Skipped Media Day, Got $200 Million — Sounds About Right
stories.body: The Pistons and Duren ended their contract standoff with a 5-year, $200 million extension after he sat out media day entirely amid the dispute. Bold negotiating strategy, and apparently it worked.

stories.headline: Missouri Crashes Florida's Party, Sends Gators Tumbling Out of the Top 10
stories.body: Missouri knocked off previously unbeaten Florida this week, handing the Gators their first loss of the season and a brutal drop in the AP rankings. The Tigers rewarded themselves with a jump to No. 14 — not a bad consolation prize for Mizzou fans who've been waiting for a moment like this.

stories.headline: Minnesota Keeps the Little Brown Jug, Michigan Has Bigger Problems Than a Jug
stories.body: Minnesota beat Michigan 20-14 to hold onto the Little Brown Jug at home for the first time since 1977 — yes, 1977. The Wolverines are in a full-blown rough patch, and losing a rivalry trophy to a team nobody was talking about this week didn't help.

stories.headline: Northwestern Rushes for 413 Yards Against Penn State Because Sure, Why Not
stories.body: Northwestern ran all over Penn State to the tune of 413 rushing yards in a win that nobody saw coming from the Wildcats' offense. It's the kind of stat line that makes you double-check the box score, then check it again.

stories.headline: Marchenko Heads to Toronto in the Season's First Blockbuster
stories.body: The Maple Leafs wasted no time making noise, acquiring Kirill Marchenko from Columbus in a deal that closed September 28 and immediately became the biggest trade of opening week. Toronto is clearly done being subtle.

stories.headline: Bedard Gets Paid: $75 Million to Stay in Chicago
stories.body: Connor Bedard locked up a five-year, $15 million AAV extension with the Blackhawks, keeping him in Chicago through the 2030-31 season. The rebuild just got a whole lot more interesting.

stories.headline: Barkov on LTIR, Panthers Already in Crisis Mode
stories.body: Florida placed Aleksander Barkov on long-term injured reserve with no clear timeline for his return, a brutal blow before the season even finds its footing. The Panthers went from Cup contender to question mark in a hurry.

stories.headline: Medvedev Beats Rublev in a Very Medvedev-vs-Rublev Final
stories.body: Daniil Medvedev claimed the Hangzhou Open title with a 7-5, 6-4 win over Andrey Rublev in an all-Russian, all-top-seed final. At this point these two should just share a trophy cabinet.

stories.headline: Rybakina and Sabalenka Sent Packing Early in Beijing
stories.body: World No. 1 Elena Rybakina and No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka both fell early at the China Open, torching the top of the draw before the tournament really got going. Chaos reigned, and Coco Gauff was happy to show up to the wreckage with a 7-6(4), 4-6, 6-2 win over Camila Osorio.

stories.headline: Alcaraz Is Back, Sinner Is Not — The Leaderboard Is Listening
stories.body: Carlos Alcaraz rolled through Tokyo with a 7-6(6), 6-1 win over Matteo Arnaldi and a walkover courtesy of Denis Shapovalov's hip injury, while Jannik Sinner sat out the China and Shanghai stretch with a lingering knee problem. The rankings picture is quietly shifting.

stories.headline: Lamine Yamal Is Now Worth More Than a Small Country's GDP
stories.body: Barcelona's Lamine Yamal hit a €225.9 million estimated transfer value this week, the highest valuation FootballTransfers has ever recorded in an October update. The kid is 17.

stories.headline: Kenan Yıldız Has Arsenal, Real Madrid, and Bayern All Sweating
stories.body: Juventus winger Kenan Yıldız has reportedly caught the eye of three of Europe's biggest clubs, with Arsenal, Real Madrid, and Bayern Munich all said to be monitoring him. Juve may want to get that contract sorted.

stories.headline: USA Puts Mexico Away 3–0 With Two Teenagers Leading the Charge
stories.body: The United States beat Mexico 3–0, with teen scorers Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall doing the damage. The future of American soccer continues to be annoyingly exciting.

stories.headline: Verstappen Finally Wins One, But Antonelli's Still Running the Show
stories.body: Max Verstappen took his first win of 2026 at the relocated Bahrain GP in Malaysia, with Antonelli crossing second and Hamilton third after a rain-delayed, software-cursed start that pushed the race back nearly two hours. Antonelli now sits 84 points clear in the championship, so Verstappen's big day was really just a footnote in someone else's title story.

stories.headline: Russell Retirement Stings as Antonelli Pulls Away
stories.body: George Russell's race-ending retirement in Malaysia couldn't have come at a worse time, handing Antonelli a clean run to a runner-up finish and an 84-point championship cushion. At this rate, Russell is going to need a lot more than a one-off PETRONAS livery to turn his season around.

stories.headline: Alonso Staying, Ocon Leaving — Aston Martin and Haas Sort Out Their Futures
stories.body: Fernando Alonso confirmed he'll remain at Aston Martin through 2027, while Haas and Esteban Ocon officially confirmed they'll split at the end of this season. Two announcements, two very different vibes.

stories.headline: 100 Starts, One Trophy: Smotherman Finally Breaks Through at Black Desert
stories.body: Austin Smotherman closed with a 3-under 68 to win the Bank of Utah Championship at 26-under 258, banking $1,080,000 in his 100th PGA Tour start. Doug Ghim finished two shots back in second — close, but not close enough to ruin a moment that was a long time coming.

stories.headline: Jarvis Holds the Keys at Dunhill Links With One Round Left
stories.body: Casey Jarvis fired a 7-under 65 at the Old Course to take a two-shot lead into the final round of the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship. Adrian Meronk's 63 kept things interesting, and Matt Fitzpatrick lurks six back — mathematically alive, realistically optimistic at best.

stories.headline: Dan Brown Shuts It Down for 2026 After Wrist Woes Derail His Season
stories.body: Dan Brown is stepping away from the PGA Tour for the remainder of 2026 after a recurring wrist injury forced a withdrawal at the BMW PGA Championship and wrecked his year. No timeline for a return has been given.
